name: Learning-Driven Autonomy Pipeline for Horizontal Wellbore Geology Prediction
authors_org: Lakshman Mahto (sole author), Quantitative Economics and Data Science, Birla Institute of Technology Mesra, Ranchi, India
venue_link: Research Square preprint (status 'In Review', not peer reviewed), DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-9902401/v1, https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-9902401/v1 (PDF: https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-9902401/v1.pdf). CITATION VERIFIED via Crossref (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.21203/rs.3.rs-9902401/v1); ordinary web search does not index it, which is why earlier searches failed.
code_availability: No code released. Four supplementary CSVs on Research Square (diagnosticmetrics.csv, uncertaintycalibrationbins.csv, rollingperformance.csv, diagnosticpredictions.csv). The data-availability statement is boilerplate about LaTeX sources, with no code or data link. License CC BY 4.0.
evidence_level: Non-peer-reviewed preprint; single-well experiment; full text read (22-page PDF). Results are invalidated by label leakage that we reproduced locally (see notes).
extreme_summary: A single-well geosteering 'autonomy' pipeline (ridge regression backbone, tree baselines, typewell GR-score, RFF kernel mean embeddings, residual sparse-attention CVAE, uncertainty-weighted fusion, steering rules) on ROGII training well 000d7d20. It reports ridge at 0.59 ft RMSE, but ridge gets that score only because it takes the train-only formation-surface columns (ANCC etc.) as inputs, and TVT is an exact linear function of Z - ANCC.
task_definition: Predict interpreted TVT for every MD station after the prediction start (first missing TVT_input; row 1,442, MD 12,909 ft) of one horizontal well. It also outputs a TVT 90% interval, a GR-score lithologic confidence, the predicted typewell layer, a favourable-layer probability, a facies-state label and a steering action (continue / up / down / hold).
inputs: Geometry: MD, X, Y, Z, horizontal distance, dZ, inclination/azimuth/curvature proxies. Log: GR plus rolling mean/std, gradient, second gradient and a missing mask. Stratigraphic: 'interpreted formation surfaces' S_i and Z - S_i. These are the ROGII train-only columns ANCC, ASTNU, ASTNL, EGFDU, EGFDL, BUDA, which the test files do not contain. Also the typewell (TVT, GR, Geology). No neighbour or sibling wells; one well only.
target_parameterisation: TVT directly for ridge/trees; the CVAE predicts the ridge residual r = TVT - TVT_ridge and GR over a 6-step horizon. No explicit dip state and no TVT + Z identity stated. The ridge implicitly learns TVT = c - (Z - ANCC) through the leaked surface features.
output_representation: Point estimate (fused TVT) with a Gaussian-style 90% interval (+-1.645 sigma_fused). The CVAE can sample multiple futures but only 6 steps ahead. No per-column depth distribution and no K hypotheses.
architecture: (1) Ridge regression on the engineered features, trained on the pre-start interval of the same well. (2) Random forest, extra trees and gradient boosting baselines. (3) Typewell GR interpolated at predicted TVT gives GR-score = exp(-(dGR/30)^2). (4) Per-modality MLP encoders, Random Fourier Features and window mean-pooling (RFF-KME, W_raw = 6) give fused tokens over L_seq = 8 windows. (5) A GRU-attention CVAE, then a causal block-sparse-attention CVAE, forecasting the ridge residual plus GR for H = 6 steps. (6) Fusion by inverse-variance or 1/RMSE^2 weights, with sigma inflated by model spread, GR std and (1 - GR-score). (7) A rule-based favourability and steering layer.
core_mechanism: Residual learning around a strong deterministic backbone: ridge carries the trend and the deep model corrects the residual. The backbone is strong only because of label leakage through the formation-surface columns. The GR-score is a pointwise typewell-consistency check used as a confidence signal, not as evidence for picking position.
training_objective: Ridge L2 least squares. CVAE ELBO: lambda_r ||r - r_hat||^2 + lambda_GR ||GR - GR_hat||^2 + beta KL(q(z|y,c) || p(z|c)). Fusion and uncertainty inflation are heuristic, not trained.
decoding: Fused prediction = weighted mean of component TVTs (precision or 1/RMSE^2 weights). The CVAE output is added to ridge. Layer comes from a typewell interval lookup and the steering action from thresholds.
metric_consistent_decode: Mean-type fusion, so nominally RMSE-consistent; it is not mode-seeking. Irrelevant in practice because the backbone leaks the label.
evidence_scope: Single well: the model is trained on that well's own heel and evaluated on its own lateral, with local rolling windows (6 x 8 samples). No multiwell training.
prefix_conditioning: The model is fit only on the known prefix (rows 0-1,441) of the same well, i.e. per-well fitting. In principle this is the most extreme form of prefix conditioning, but here it only calibrates the leaked Z - surface relation.
propose_vs_select: Single output from a fixed-weight fusion of components. Not a candidate generator in any useful sense for us.
physical_constraints: None imposed explicitly. The leaked surface features encode the TVT + Z - ANCC identity by construction.
dataset: [uncertain: region] One ROGII Kaggle training well, identified locally as 000d7d20: 5,278 rows, 1,296-row typewell, PS at row 1,442 / MD 12,909 ft; the first id in sample_submission is 000d7d20_1442. Region presumably the same US onshore basin as the competition. No other wells.
synthetic_to_real: No synthetic data. No normalisation between lateral and typewell beyond a fixed s_GR = 30 API in the GR-score. No alignment stage.
metric_and_performance: Table 1 (forward interval, one well): ridge RMSE 0.5876 ft, MAE 0.5129, bias -0.4628, R2 0.9867. 'gr_match' has identical numbers (a likely copy or pass-through bug). Uncertainty-fused 0.6389. Extra trees 5.39, random forest 7.99, gradient boosting 19.55 ft. Our local check on the same well: a linear fit on Z - ANCC trained on the prefix gives 0.007 ft; all six surfaces + Z give 0.042 ft; geometry only (MD, X, Y, Z) gives 58.9 ft; last-value carry-forward gives 7.45 ft.
comparability: Not comparable. One well versus our 155; it uses train-only interpreted surfaces that do not exist at test time (a label proxy); there is no cross-well generalisation. An inference-legal version would be the geometry-only or last-value numbers (58.9 / 7.45 ft on this well), far worse than our 4.84 ft pooled.
validation_protocol: Single temporal split within one well (prefix train, lateral test). No well-level CV, no leaderboard. Section 7 recommends well-ID splits and train-only normalisation for future multiwell work, but none was done.
inference_budget: Trivial (ridge plus a small CVAE on one well). Not reported.
repeated_layers: Not handled. The GR-score is pointwise and unimodal, and it would score a wrong repeated band as high confidence. The author lists windowed or DTW-based lithologic confidence as future work.
drift: Not handled explicitly. Within one well the leaked surfaces remove drift entirely; with legal inputs, a ridge on geometry extrapolates linearly and diverges (58.9 ft on this well in our check).
uncertainty_and_calibration: Heuristic sigma_fused = sqrt(sigma_resid^2 + spread^2) * (1 + lambda_noise*GR_std/30 + lambda_GR*(1 - GR-score)), with a Gaussian 90% interval. There is a reliability-style plot (Fig. 5: predicted sigma bins vs observed |error| and empirical 90% coverage), but numbers are only in the supplementary CSV. No temperature/isotonic calibration and no ECE. It explicitly notes that fusion underestimates uncertainty when components share a bias.
where_to_use: Only as reporting and presentation inspiration (the lit-review's intended use): rolling-RMSE-along-MD plots, error by typewell layer, calibration-by-sigma-bin plots, and GR-score versus uncertainty. Also as a cautionary citation showing that the ROGII train files contain label-proxy surface columns, and why any paper using them must be read critically. Not a model component.
error_mode_targeted: None of ours (band confusion, drift, broad hump). Relevant only to measurement/protocol, as an example of leakage.
gap_vs_our_implementation: [uncertain: whether items (b) and the loader audit are already covered] No methodological gap. Everything it offers is weaker than what we already have: a multiwell-trained per-column posterior with expectation decode versus a single-well ridge. Reporting items we could adopt: (a) per-typewell-layer error breakdown; (b) a reliability plot of predicted spread versus observed |error| with empirical interval coverage for our posterior (useful for the calibration lever named in the context); (c) a pointwise GR-consistency score, GR_obs - GR_typewell(TVT_hat), as a cheap diagnostic of which wells are catastrophic. Protocol confirmation: our loaders must never read ANCC/ASTNU/ASTNL/EGFDU/EGFDL/BUDA as holdout-time model inputs, because TVT + Z - ANCC is constant to 0.005 ft within a well (verified on 000d7d20). They are legitimate only as training-time targets or augmentation devices (as used by the 1st/2nd place synthetic pipelines).
proposed_experiment: No model experiment is recommended. Two cheap hygiene/reporting tasks. (1) Leakage audit: grep the data loaders (kaggle_1st_place/solution/experiments/*/seq_NN_*.py, kaggle2ndplace/src/*, rogii_champion/src/*) for ANCC|ASTNU|ASTNL|EGFDU|EGFDL|BUDA and assert that none reaches a holdout-time input tensor. Add a unit test that zeroes those columns for holdout wells and checks the predictions are bit-identical. (2) A reliability figure for the paper: from seq_NN_posterior_dump.py --save-all outputs, bin rows by posterior std (deciles) and plot the RMS error per bin against the mean std, plus empirical coverage of the posterior 90% interval, for the ConvNeXt teacher and the FastViT student. Report ECE-style gaps. This directly quantifies the calibration lever. Control: none needed, since it is analysis only.
implementation_effort: Low: the audit is a grep plus a single test; the reliability plot is about 50 lines over existing posterior dumps.
gpu_cost: None (CPU analysis over existing posterior dumps).
distillation_compatibility: Not applicable (no model to distil). The reliability analysis applies to both teacher and student posteriors.
error_correlation_with_ours: Not applicable. An inference-legal version (geometry ridge) would be far too inaccurate (tens of ft) to earn blend weight.
risk: Citing it as evidence that 'TVT is mostly geometry-controlled' would be wrong and could embarrass our write-up. The conclusion is an artefact of feeding interpreted formation surfaces (a direct function of the label) to the model. It is a single well, has no multiwell validation, and 'gr_match' has metrics identical to ridge (suspect code). No code is available to check further.
notes: [uncertain: exact cause of 0.59 vs 0.007 ft] Citation verified: Mahto, L. (2026). Learning-Driven Autonomy Pipeline for Horizontal Wellbore Geology Prediction. Research Square preprint, doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-9902401/v1, posted 2026-07-20. Local leakage check on kaggle_1st_place/solution/data/train/000d7d20__horizontal_well.csv: the train file has columns MD,X,Y,Z,ANCC,ASTNU,ASTNL,EGFDU,EGFDL,BUDA,TVT,GR,TVT_input, while the test file has only MD,X,Y,Z,GR,TVT_input. TVT + Z - ANCC = 11373.22-11373.27 over the whole well (std 0.005 ft post-PS). A one-feature fit on Z - ANCC gives 0.007 ft. The paper's 0.59 ft (with a -0.46 ft bias) is consistent with a regularised ridge over many correlated features. It agrees with the lit-review note that the work is 'not very scientifically done'; it is useful only for figure ideas. Research Square pages are not indexed by general web search; use Crossref or the DOI to find it.
